speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Ministry will review the relevant legislation to enhance the sentences for all types of sexual offences, with or without penetration and with or without violence, committed on minors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Ms Tin is asking me to prejudge the review before the review takes place.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There would not be a review asked if we felt that everything was okay as it is.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I should not jump in and say it is definitely going to go in a certain direction because, as I had said, we need to look at it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Perhaps, in some situations, the laws may be adequate but some processes, in terms of which charges to prefer or which charges to look at, that is not within the control of the Government.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Which charges to prefer and how to proceed is an independent decision by the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC).

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But as a matter of policy, we may need to have discussions with AGC without having to deal with individual cases.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I speak personally here, without having to prejudge the issue.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think that, in two areas, in the context of vulnerable victims, very young children who are subjected to sexual abuse, who are preyed upon, or who otherwise would have had.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And there is a separate class of vulnerable victims, and by no means is this comprehensive; domestic helpers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They come here and do the work because we do not have enough people.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But they have to be treated with a certain dignity and a certain respect for the law.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if they are ill-treated to the extent where they suffer physical and mental torture, I think we also look at that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The laws already provide for punishments to be enhanced in the context of some vulnerable victims.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How that is to be arrived at, like I said, whether you have to necessarily legislate or you have to relook at some of the processes, policies, that is something that is part of the review.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I check whether they will be including the mentally disabled as well?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We would be looking at many of these issues.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am not going to comment as to whether we will specifically be looking at the mentally disabled.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I think Members can assume that we are doing quite a comprehensive review.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Will the Ministry be considering any public consultation for this process?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Specifically for the vulnerable victims and the children.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not want to commit my officials before we have crossed the bridge, but public consultation is something that we do quite frequently when it comes to these sorts of laws.
